rationale: Luke 12:22-32 is a fuller running parallel to Matthew 6:25-33, close enough in places to be word-for-word identical in this app's own shipped BSB text -- 'Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?' appears verbatim at both 6:27 and 12:25 -- while diverging in several specific, checkable ways elsewhere. Matthew's 'birds of the air' (6:26, BSB) becomes Luke's 'ravens' (12:24, BSB), a named, ritually unclean bird under the law (Leviticus 11:13-15; Deuteronomy 14:12-14), a sharper example than Matthew's general category. Matthew's threefold rhetorical question, 'What shall we eat?... What shall we drink?... What shall we wear?' (6:31, BSB), becomes Luke's flatter instruction not to 'be concerned about what you will eat or drink' (12:29, BSB), with clothing addressed separately at 12:22 rather than inside the same triad. Matthew's conclusion, 'seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you' (6:33, BSB), becomes Luke's shorter 'seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you' (12:31, BSB) -- Luke's wording drops 'first,' 'of God,' and 'and His righteousness' outright, a real difference worth stating plainly rather than treating the two verses as interchangeable. Luke alone adds a further verse with no parallel in Matthew's unit at all: 'Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom' (12:32, BSB). The type is parallel because both texts record the same core teaching on worry and provision without either naming or quoting the other by formula; the label is strong because the shared and the differing wording are both directly checkable against both Gospels' own shipped text, including at least two lines that match exactly.
